header: DO NOT EDIT: regenerate with `python3 proofs/verus/gen_pin_tests.py <spec> --run`.
Each test mirrors one [pins] row of proofs/verus/shir_native_command_noop_cond_sync.txt
and drives the REAL fold (`native_command_noop_cond`), not a copy of it.
The `cnn_bash_*` and d3 rows measure the shell's own answer with bash, so the
law's premise (an empty redirect target always fails) and both recorded
divergences rest on observed behaviour, not on the model's say-so.

pins.note: `if command <'' >''` — the redirect can never open, so bash's status is 1 and the plain condition is false; the fold writes Bool(false)
`if ! command <'' >''` — the same failing redirect under `!` is true, and the fold writes Bool(true)
`! command -v ls >''` keeps the shell-out: the answer depends on the WORD (and on whether ls resolves), so no constant may be written — measured below
`if ! command -v ls` has no `redirect` Call at all, so the fold's first shape gate refuses it
`if printf x >''` is a different program: the fold requires the command word to be `command`
a redirect whose body is TWO statements runs between the redirect and the status the fold claims, so it is refused
d3a: `if command > /dev/null` — the redirect SUCCEEDS and `command` exits 0, so bash's condition is true while the fold writes false
d3b: `if ! command <$IN >$OUT` (the corpus' lex-dot-in-var.sh) — with openable files bash's `!` is false, the fold writes true
the law's premise, measured: `command <'' >''` exits 1 and `! command <'' >''` exits 0 in bash
